references.text: Moses' objection to God continues from his earlier hesitation at the burning bush, where he also questioned his own worthiness for the task.
Moses repeats his objection that he has uncircumcised lips, which corresponds to his claim of being slow of speech and tongue.
Moses uses the same argument about his uncircumcised lips as a reason why Pharaoh will not listen to him.
Isaiah expresses similar concern about his unclean lips when he encounters God's holiness.
Jeremiah also objects to his calling by saying that he cannot speak because he is young, similar to Moses' resistance.
The psalm refers to God who spoke to Israel in Egypt, where Moses was the mouthpiece despite his reluctance.
Stephen tells that Moses was mighty in word and deed, showing that God overcame Moses' speech impediment.
Contrast between Moses' experienced speech difficulties and God's confirmation that He speaks 'mouth to mouth' with him.
God's direct command to speak (6:29) answers Moses' objection about not being a 'man of words' (4:10).
